title: Patience, again
hook: patience in obedience, patience from sin, patience in trials

segments.voice: Yesterday, zuhd, detachment, and your line: not owned by it. Today, a station we've met before, opened up.

Three people, same morning. The first is getting out of a warm bed in the dark for the dawn prayer, and every part of her wants to stay. The second is scrolling when a message arrives he knows he shouldn't answer the way he wants to. The third is in a hospital corridor, waiting for a door to open with news. Teachers of the inward path would give all three the same name. Patience. Not one patience, they say, but three.
screen: `OUT OF A WARM BED.` → `A MESSAGE NOT TO ANSWER.` → `A HOSPITAL CORRIDOR.`

segments.voice: In Arabic, patience is sabr. In Pickthall's translation, the Qur'an says: "O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast." Steadfastness is a good clue. Sabr isn't sitting still; it's holding steady. Scholars of the inward path describe three kinds. Patience in obedience: keeping on with a good thing when it's hard, the woman getting out of bed. Patience from sin: holding back from a wrong thing when it's tempting, the man not hitting send. And patience in trials: staying steady when something hits you that you didn't choose, the person in the corridor. A person can be strong in one and thin in another. Someone who never misses a prayer can still fire off the angry message. Someone calm in a crisis can still struggle with the alarm clock. Then a moment in Sahih al-Bukhari. The Prophet ﷺ passes a woman weeping at a grave and tells her to be patient. She doesn't recognize him and snaps that he hasn't been struck by what she has. Later she learns who it was, and comes to his door to explain. He doesn't scold her. He says, in effect, that patience is at the first blow. Not the weeping; the first moment. This week's stations, good character, the Revival, turning back, watchfulness, the evening ledger, detachment, each need this one to last. And if a loss ever feels too heavy to hold alone, you don't have to: in the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.
screen: `SABR: HOLDING STEADY.` · `IN OBEDIENCE, FROM SIN, IN TRIALS.` · `PATIENCE IS AT THE FIRST BLOW.` · `A WEEK OF STATIONS.`

segments.voice: Hold up the three, keeping on with a good thing, holding back from a wrong one, staying steady in something hard, and ask which is thinnest in your life right now. Picture the first moment it will be tested, the alarm, the reply, the waiting room, and picture yourself holding steady for just that moment. If you pray, you can rest on the line: Allah is with the steadfast.
Patience. Sabr: holding steady, in doing good, in holding back from wrong, and in what life brings. Today's word.
Your line: three patiences. Each of them begins with just the first moment. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims speak of sabr in three kinds: in keeping up acts of worship, in holding back from wrongdoing, and in bearing hardship; people often remind one another to have sabr in times of loss.
